column1: # fa.spoken.words.tsv -- the whole-word table of the Persian colloquial normaliser (lib/spoken.py).
# One row per spoken word or phrase.  Tab-separated, UTF-8, `#` starts a comment, the first row is the header.
#   spoken   the word as speech writes it (a phrase has its words apart, one space between)
#   formal   the formal word it stands for; for a `standalone` row, the word itself
#   kind     word | phrase | formula | cv | standalone | policy
#              word        one spoken word for a formal word (or for two: `هیچ جا`, read word by word)
#              phrase      several spoken words for a formal word or phrase
#              formula     a fixed expression, read word by word, with its meaning as a whole
#              cv          the spoken first part of a compound verb (نیگا کن = نگاه کردن)
#              standalone  a colloquial word the dictionary has no formal twin for: its gloss is the answer
#              policy      a word the dictionary knows that speech also reads another way (رفتن: they went): no formal word of
#                          its own, only `show`: what the endings of the rule file find for it is shown beside the
#                          dictionary's own answer when the row says so
#   flags    comma-separated: certain (only speech writes it: counts as spoken evidence for its neighbours),
#            show=always|spoken|never (when the spoken reading stands beside a direct dictionary hit of the
#            same word; default never), likelier=spoken (first, not second, where it is shown),
#            pos=<part of speech of a standalone word>, with=<infinitive of a cv's light verb>,
#            needs=spoken (the row applies only where the chunk says it is speech -- the page's hint, or a word beside it that only
#            speech writes: a one-letter word like ب for به, or a word that is speech's only by its neighbours, بسم)
#   gloss    what the word or formula means, in English: required for `standalone` and `formula`
#   note     the reason in words, where "spoken for X" is not enough
#   src      hazm (reviewed pairs of Hazm's iwords.dat, MIT: see fa.spoken.HAZM-LICENSE.txt) | note | own
# A row counts only where the dictionary has the formal word (standalone rows excepted): the table adds
# lookup routes and never a word the dictionary does not stand behind.
